title: Describing a Robot Once: One Text File With a Source for Every Number, and Two Models Made From It, the Built In One and the SDF

questions.question: What does the word typical in a robot file mean?
options: The number is an average of several sources
The number was measured on a typical robot
The number was not found; it is a value for a robot of this class
The number may be ignored
questions.explanation: Where a figure could be found the file says where. Where it could not, the file says typical, so a reader knows which numbers to check first.

questions.question: How many of the 11 numbers of the reference robot are typical?
questions.explanation: Eight carry a source and three are marked typical. The file makes it plain which are which.

questions.question: The masses of the links in the SDF added up to:
options: 1.060 kg, the body plus the wheels
1.000 kg, the robot's mass
questions.explanation: The body is given what is left after the wheels and the caster. A body that took the whole mass and then had wheels added would weigh too much.

questions.question: What is a line with a number and no source?
options: Refused at its line
Accepted, and marked typical
Accepted with a warning
Read as zero
questions.explanation: The parser refuses it and names the line. A number nobody can trace is one whose difference from the real robot cannot be found.

questions.question: Why generate both models from one file?
options: One file is easier to read
Two copies of a dimension will eventually disagree, and neither simulator will say so
The simulators require the same format
It halves the build time
questions.explanation: Kept in two places, the track width gets changed in one. Both simulators run happily on their own copy and disagree with each other.

questions.question: Why compute inertias from the shapes?
options: Gazebo refuses a model without them
Shapes are easier to type than numbers
To make the model heavier
A default inertia is a robot that spins or turns wrongly
questions.explanation: A box of 1 kg with these sides has an Ixx of 0.00511 kg m2. A made up inertia gives a robot that turns too easily or too stiffly, with no error.
